sources.citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2014. Dogon lexical tones of stems (cross-Dogon typological note, last update December 2014). 6 pp., dogonlanguages.org.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Mombo stress. p.3: 'In southwestern Dogon (Bunoge, Penange, Ampari, Mombo) and in Tiranige (northwestern), all verb forms have tones that are predictable from the inflectional form, so there are no lexical melodies.' Only Donno So is described as moving toward a pitch accent system.

sources.citation: Prokhorov, Kirill. 2012. A Grammar of Mombo, Songho Dialect (Dogon language family, Mali). Draft dated September 2012, ix+275 pp., posted on dogonlanguages.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The phonology chapter exists only as sec. 3.2.2 (metrical/moraic structure of bisyllabic stems with CC clusters: 'short' <=2 morae vs 'long' stems, used to predict {H} vs {HL} tone overlays) and sec. 3.7.2 (grammatical tone patterns and thematic vowels of verbs). Nouns have lexical tone classes {H},{HL},{LH}; verb tones are grammatically assigned. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 285-page draft; chapters 1-2 and the rest of ch. 3 (segments, tone sandhi, intonation) are unwritten.
